To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integration of planning problems of the transportation and the electrical energy sector can be beneficial and that the number of charging stations as well as the size of the storage capacity can be determined by means of an integrated planning approach.
the integration of battery electric vehicles into the energy sector leads to new challenges and opportunities for the planning of charging infrastructure.

an integrated planning of charging infrastructure and the electrical grid can be used to exploit the potential of battery electric vehicles in terms of load flow control and that this can be achieved by installing charging stations and storage capacity in the right locations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of two planning problems that have not been integrated so far.
the planning and operation of charging infrastructure for electric vehicles considering load flows in the electrical grid.
the development of an integrated location model for the planning of charging stations and the planning of load flow control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
an integrated planning approach is necessary for the planning of charging infrastructure for battery-electric vehicles and the electrical grid.
an integrated approach is necessary to exploit synergies of both sectors.
the integrated planning approach leads to a better network configuration than the planning of the sectors separately, as it is done in practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
an integrated planning approach is needed to exploit potential synergistic effects between both sectors.

our results show that a higher number of charging stations and an increased storage capacity can lead to higher costs for the energy provider, but at the same time to a reduction in the number of vehicles on the road.
the integration of the two sectors is beneficial and that a high number of charging stations and a large amount of storage capacity are needed to exploit the potential synergies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a joint planning of charging station locations and storage capacities can significantly reduce the required storage capacity and thus, the investment costs for the electrical grid.
the integration of planning problems for charging infrastructure and load flow control can be a promising approach for a sustainable and efficient planning of the transportation and energy sector.
a high installed storage capacity can reduce the need for charging infrastructure.
